preamble: Palatalized [tʲ] (from *t before *j) developed into the postalveolar fricative [ʃ] in Latvian and Latgalian, where Proto-Baltic *tj regularly gives š, while Lithuanian keeps an affricate č [tʃ] in the same words (Latvian svešs vs Lithuanian svẽčias). The change is otherwise rare; the usual outcome of palatalized [tʲ] is an affricate.

examples.note: Cognate with Lithuanian svẽčias 'foreign' and svetỹs 'guest', which show the affricate č where Latvian has š.
Compare Latvian trešais and Lithuanian trečias 'third', from Proto-Indo-European *tritós.
